message.projecthero.doctor_fate.possesse: Nabu has taken your body. Your mind is trapped in his library: convince him to let you go.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.released: Nabu lets you go. You're back in your body; the helmet falls from your head and won't go back on for 60 s.
hud.projecthero.doctor_fate.possessed_hi: Your mind is being drawn into Nabu's library...
item.projecthero.helmet_of_fate.tip.drop: Dropped, it hovers where it lands.
projecthero.doctor_fate.ability.helmet.d: Wearing it: take it off (you lift it over your head and get the Helmet of Fate item). Not wearing it: summon it from wherever it is (set down, dropped, in a chest, someone's inventory, another dimension, far away) and it flies to you and goes on. Shift+right-click the item to wear it, right-click a block to set it down; dropped, it lands and hovers there. It can't come off during a Possession and won't go on for 60 s after one.
projecthero.doctor_fate.ability.flight.d: Helmet on: golden-ankh hover flight, cloak billowing. 14 blocks a second, 28 sprinting, a still hover with no keys. Double-tap Space again to drop. You never take fall damage with the helmet on.
projecthero.guide.doctor_fate.helmet.bod: Your powers come from the helmet: with it off you have none, just normal health, and Dominion slowly drains. Wearing it: 40 health, 30% damage resistance, +8 melee damage, Regeneration I, flight (double-tap Space), no fall damage, immunity to Wither and Poison, and every spell. You can't wear armour with it: whatever you had on goes to your inventory, and armour won't go on while it's on. Putting it on, you raise the helmet in both hands, hold it high while a golden ankh flares behind it and lower it onto your head; the golden helmet, the Cloak of Destiny and the Amulet of Anubis appear. H takes it off and gives you the Helmet of Fate item. Shift+right-click the item to wear it again, or right-click a block to set it down: it hovers there, glowing (right-click to pick it up). Drop it (Q, a full inventory, dying) and it doesn't stay an item: it flies on, lands and hovers where it lands, the same way. Fire, lava and explosions can't touch it. Shift+H still opens the power wheel.
projecthero.guide.doctor_fate.summon.bod: With the helmet off, press H and it comes to you from wherever it is: set down on a block, dropped, in a chest, an ender chest, another player's inventory, in another dimension or in a chunk nobody has loaded. If it's near, it flies out of where it lay along a golden trail into your raised hand; otherwise a golden ankh portal opens beside you and it comes out of that. Then you put it on. There is only ever one: the copy it left behind is gone (an old copy in a place nobody could see disappears the moment that place loads). During the 60 s after a Possession it lands in your inventory instead.
projecthero.guide.doctor_fate.possession: At 100 Dominion Nabu takes your body, and there is no time limit: it lasts until you convince him to let you go. Your body fights on in the world with twice your strength, casting at every player nearby (whatever they have or haven't done) and every hostile creature, never squadmates, villagers, golems or tamed animals, and it can't die while he holds it (not even in the void). Your mind is trapped in his library (below). When he lets you go you're back in your body where it stands; the helmet falls from your head and lands on the ground, it can't go back on for 60 s (H brings it to your inventory meanwhile), and Dominion settles at 70. Logging out doesn't free you: you're still his when you come back, and the trial starts again.
projecthero.guide.doctor_fate.library.bo: You arrive at the end of a long sandstone hallway; the door behind you slams shut. At its end a great round library: walls of books four tiers high, twelve lecterns in a ring, the Eye of Nabu burning at its heart and a huge screen on the far wall showing what your body sees. Walk with WASD and the mouse. 1. The pages: three of the twelve lecterns hold a page of Kent Nelson's journal; the rest hold Nabu's tomes, and every tome you read angers him. Right-click (or R) at a lectern to read it. Unread books glow gold, Kent's pages blue once read. 2. The challenges: with all three pages, right-click at the Eye. Nabu challenges you once for each page, with three answers; only the one that page argues is right. A wrong answer angers him and tears that page away to another lectern: find it again. 3. The will: once every challenge is won, face him again. He pushes on your mind: tap Space to hold your will inside the blue band that wanders up and down. Hold it there for 10 s and he lets you go; drift out of it for 3 s and he wins that round, re-opens one challenge and grows angrier. His anger bar fills with every mistake; when it's full his wrath scatters everything (new lecterns, every page and challenge lost) and your body lashes out. You can re-read a page any time.
projecthero.guide.doctor_fate.bargains.b: Nabu offers deals on a small two-button screen that doesn't pause the game. You have 10 s to choose, and ignoring one counts as refusing. Death's door (3 hearts or fewer, or a blow that would kill you): full heal and a golden shield for +35 Dominion; while it's on screen nothing can hurt you, so you can't die before you choose. Order's command (sometimes at night): banish 5 creatures of Chaos before dawn for -30 Dominion and an Ankh Charm, or +40 if you fail. Forbidden spell: Shift+Z always asks first, and Nabu always says yes, but Dominion goes to 90+. Each refusal makes his next offer that day meaner: bigger reward, bigger cost.
projecthero.guide.doctor_fate.fair.body: Possession never attacks squadmates. On a server you can't be possessed inside spawn protection. Banishment never deletes bosses or players. No fall damage with the helmet on, while possessed, or in the 60 s after.
screen.projecthero.doctor_fate.bargain.d: Nabu holds death back while you choose: nothing can hurt you until you answer.
hud.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.title: NABU HOLDS YOU
Find Kent Nelson's pages among Nabu's tomes (%s of %s). Every tome angers him.
You have the pages. Face Nabu at the Eye and answer his challenges.
Every challenge won. Face Nabu at the Eye: hold your will against his.
hud.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.will_h: Tap SPACE to hold your will in the blue band
hud.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.zone.e: The Eye of Nabu. Right-click (or R) to face him.
hud.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.zone.l: A book. Right-click (or R) to read it.
Already read. Right-click (or R) to read it again.
hud.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.zone.h: Walk to a lectern or to the Eye at the library's heart.
There is no way back. Walk on.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.su: Convince him, or stay his forever
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.be: Your body is mine now, Kent Nelson's heir. Walk my halls. Argue, if you think you can. Nobody leaves until I allow it.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.do: The door is shut behind you. There is only forward.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.to: My words, not his. You waste my patience.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.pa: So. You found the old man's scribblings. Come to the Eye and face me.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.em: You come before me with %s of %s pages? Read, mortal, if you can tell his words from mine.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.ri: ...True. That is his argument, and it has weight. Go on.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.al: Words, words. Now let me feel your will. Face me again.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.wr: Wrong. You don't even know your own case. I take that page from you: find it again.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.wi: Push against me, then. Hold, if you can.
Your will breaks like glass. We are not done talking.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.wr: ENOUGH! Everything you gathered is ash. Begin again.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.fr: ...Very well. Take your body back. For now.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.ta: Do you hear it? Your body fights so much better without you.
Kent Nelson tried this too. He was patient. Are you?
There is no clock in this place. I can wait forever.
Order is kept while you wander my shelves.
Every book here is mine. Almost every book.
Watch the screen, mortal. That is what you could be.
The doors do not open from your side.
Your hands strike, your mouth commands, and none of it is you.
I have outlived kings. I will outlive your patience.
Chaos stirs out there. Why would I give this body back?
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.pa: A page of Kent Nelson's journal. Remember what it argues: Nabu will test you on it.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.to: One of Nabu's tomes. Reading it angered him.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.an: 1-3 or click to answer, Esc to step back
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.pa: Order without choice is only a cage. Even the Lords of Order were not made to serve by chains: they chose Order. A helmet that takes the choice away has stopped serving Order at all.
Nabu forgets this each time: a vessel with no mind of its own breaks. A hollow body serves him a season and then fails. He needs his host whole, the mind as well as the hands.
I took the helmet off for the people I loved. Order that harms the innocent is only Chaos wearing gold. A Lord of Order who strikes at everyone near has already lost.
Order and Chaos are two pans of one scale. When Order devours everything, the scale tips, and the tipping itself wakes Chaos. Too much Order is how the Lords of Chaos return.
The oath we swore in the Tower of Fate, Nabu and I: I wear the helmet; the helmet does not wear me. He agreed to it. He will not like being reminded, but he agreed.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.to: The vessel exists to obey. Its wishes are noise. Its silence is the first step toward Order.
Codex of Nabu: The weak hand
Mortal hands tremble. Mortal hearts hesitate. A Lord of Order hesitates at nothing, and so a Lord of Order must hold the hand.
Mercy is a door left open for Chaos. Close every door.
Codex of Nabu: The long count
I have counted the ages since the first host. Each lasted a moment. Each thought it mattered.
Codex of Nabu: The perfect form
Order is perfection, and perfection does not bargain with the imperfect.
The Tower of Fate stands outside time. So do I. The vessel does not. Remember which of us will remain.
All who stand near the vessel are judged. Their deeds do not matter. Their nearness is enough.
The page is blank but for one word, written over and over: SILENCE.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.qu: Order is perfect. Why should perfection kneel to one mortal's wish?
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.an: Because Order without choice is only a cage.
Because I'm stronger than you are.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.qu: This body serves me better than you ever did. Why should I return it?
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.an: A hollow vessel breaks. You need my mind whole.
Because the helmet belongs to me by right.
Because you'll grow bored of it.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.qu: I strike down everyone who stands near. Is that not justice?
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.an: Order that harms the innocent is Chaos wearing gold.
Only if they've done wrong before.
Justice is whatever the strong decide.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.qu: Then why not let Order rule forever, through me?
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.an: Too much Order tips the scale and wakes Chaos.
Because forever is too long to wait.
Because Chaos is the better master.
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.qu: What did your kind promise me, mortal?
message.projecthero.doctor_fate.trial.an: That I wear the helmet; the helmet does not wear me.
To give you my body whenever you ask.
